english.title: Estate Agent / property developer make a false statement about prescribed matters relating to land
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the person carrying on

(A)_[an estate agency]_
(B)_[a property development]_

business, made a false or misleading statement, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FALSE OR MISLEADING STATEMENT..), in the course of that business about a prescribed matter
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1 of the Property Misdescriptions Act 1991.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being the person carrying on an estate agency / property development business
made a false or misleading statement
in the course of that business
about a prescribed matter

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The Property Misdescriptions (Specified Matters) Order 1992 (S.I. 1992/2834) sets out the prescribed matters.
(ii) Section 5 of the Property Misdescriptions Act 1991 provides that the time limit on prosecutions is three years beginning with the date of commission of the offence or the end of the period of one year beginning with the date of the discovery of the offence by the prosecutor, whichever is the earlier.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
